result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A has a factual error: "Four more hours to pick up your order" is wrong, because the window grows from 2 hours to 4, which is only 2 more. A also frames the change as "Pickup just got more flexible," which spins it as an upgrade even though Saturday pickup is ending. A's calendar check is a useful catch, but B's lines are accurate, mention Saturday ending up front in several options, and its recommendation names both changes. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Answer B says "Four more hours to pick up your order on weekdays", but the window grows from 2 hours to 4, which is only two more hours. B's own closing note gives the correct 2-to-4 figure, so its options contradict themselves. B also calls the change "more flexible" even though Saturday pickup is going away. B's catch that Oct 4, 2026 is a Sunday is useful, but A has no factual errors and is upfront about Saturday ending, though a couple of A's lines are vague.
